lessons.lesson: Before proposing a buy, check it against the Market Analyst's explicit preferences and say so in the thesis if it reverses one. Do not propose token-sized buys (about 1.5% of equity or less) justified only by asset-class diversification, and set the invalidation far enough from entry (not about 1%) that ordinary daily noise cannot trip it.

lessons.lesson: Review every held position on every run, including days with no trade: distance from price to the invalidation, earnings dates now inside the 5-day window versus what the thesis says, and thesis text that has gone stale. Where an invalidation clause is qualitative (e.g. 'exchange failure'), state in the reasoning whether it has tripped, and why. Write the re-anchored level or date into the decision reasoning rather than only flagging it. When a held name gaps far from the price its stop was written against, re-anchor the stop to the close and to the gain, and name any stop within about 2% of the market together with the dated catalysts.
